protocol: Use the frozen, pooled audio branch of facebook/pe-av-large and CLAP on equal original channels, the same entire 5 s and the same text prompts ("the sound of "+category with underscores replaced by spaces). Select the highest-scoring phrase in each encoder. The initial protocol called both scores cosine. PE-AV uses its unnormalized audio-text dot product as in its published forward pass; CLAP uses cosine. First use the already selected 50 previously unused recordings as a feasibility set. Then evaluate the same fixed method on two further originals per class, preferring folds 2 and 4, without reusing any source file ID. Do not tune weights, prompts or a rejection threshold. Keep open caption scores and closed vocabulary discrimination separate. With known silence do not query either encoder. Results cannot establish every mentioned sound is present.
selection_note: One class had no further unused original for its second file. All 99 available distinct originals in the selected pairs were scored. Selection excluded prior project files by source ID. The 50 and 99 sets share neither an original nor a clip. Model pretraining overlap unknown.
scoring: One recorded mono channel, five seconds in full. Same list of 50 English source names. Nearest choice by cosine. Agreement with the target omitted is reconstructed from already computed top-three rankings, with no change to the recording. Another sound can be incidental; absence in this test means the labelled target was excluded from the offered set.
